data_fields.name: turn_in_material_amount
data_fields.donor_constant: per MakeItem Material Amount attribute in Quest.xml (e.g. 1 in the cloak turn-in)

data_fields.name: turn_in_reward_amount
data_fields.donor_constant: per MakeItem Item Amount attribute in Quest.xml (e.g. 1 in the cloak turn-in)

data_fields.name: quest_gate_step
data_fields.donor_constant: per QuestStep attribute in Quest.xml (0, 1, 2 ...; -1 means any started quest)

data_fields.name: listed_child_order
data_fields.donor_constant: document order; each child gate read at its own turn (donor); snapshot in sketch

best_idea: A quest is a per-character integer step with an END value, and every NPC line is a data row gated on npc, level, class and step, with a Succeed or Fail branch for item turn-ins.
decision_why: Keep the data-gated NPC action tree and the per-character step log, which fit zones-as-data and the one-ledger ruling; fix the donor's null map at login, the memory write after a failed SQL write, the Java-hardcoded quest branches and the order-dependent sibling gates before building.
acceptance: Server test: a player at step 1 turns in the item; materials are consumed, the reward is granted and the step moves to END in one server transaction; a forced DB write failure leaves the in-memory step unchanged; a fresh login's first SetQuest runs without a prior gate call.
